subject: Discovery follow-up: streaming bottlenecks and p95/concurrency goals (DataWorks)
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@dataworks.io>, dataworks-ops@dataworks.io
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: streaming bottlenecks and p95/concurrency goals (DataWorks)

Hi Ethan (and team),

Thanks again for the 45-minute call today — appreciated the level of detail on the production issues. Short recap to align on what we heard and the proposed next steps. Please flag anything I missed.

Pain points (what you told us)
- Production streaming responses are intermittently exceeding p95 targets (~1.0–1.4s currently for 512-token sessions).
- UX: partial tokens arrive in bursts rather than a steady stream; front-end experiences stalls during prefix changes.
- Concurrency: sustained load around 200–300 concurrent streaming sessions during peaks; burst to ~500 for 30–45s.
- Cost: current infra (on-prem Triton + homegrown autoscaler) is opaque and hard to right-size.

Current stack summary (as called out)
- Triton-inference behind NGINX LB; requests flow through a service that manages KV cache for prompt prefixes.
- 1–2x GPU hosts per region (A100 gen1).

Success criteria for a PoC/trial
- p95 streaming response latency <= 300ms for 512-token streaming requests (US region).
- Support for steady streaming semantics (partial tokens within <50ms of generation where possible).
- Sustained concurrency handling of 300 sessions with headroom for 500 burst.
- No change to data residency (keep US region), and ability to integrate with your KMS for keying (we can sign NDAs/DPAs first).

Immediate asks / next steps
1) We (Redwood) will propose a 2-week technical trial: dedicated capacity + sample traffic to reproduce the p95 issue.
2) Can you share: a) sample payloads (we attached sample_payloads.zip), b) a short DVR of a failing streaming session (if possible), and c) QPS/latency CSV for last 7 days?
3) Let us know any constraints for SOC2/KMS/procurement before we spin up a private trial.
4) Proposed: 30-min technical kickoff next Tue/Wed to finalize bench config.

I'll loop in our Solutions and CS leads so we can draft a trial plan and a ballpark quote.

Thanks,

Aisha Rahman
Enterprise Solutions (West)
Redwood Inference
aisha.rahman@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

Attachments: sample_payloads.zip (payloads + minimal harness)
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@dataworks.io>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: dataworks-ops@dataworks.io
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 16:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: streaming bottlenecks and p95/concurrency goals (DataWorks)

Thanks Aisha — solid recap and yes, that matches what we saw. A couple clarifications from our side:

- The 1.0–1.4s p95 number is for our 512-token prompt baseline; the median is ~220ms. The issue is the tail on partial token emission when requests hit a cache miss or when backend batching triggers.
- The bursts to 500 are typically during model previews (marketing events) and last 20–45s. Those bursts are where UX complaints spike.
- We rely on incremental partial chunks (the FE expects ~50–100ms cadence). If the inference layer batches tokens and flushes in 400–800ms chunks we get the front-end stalls.

I've attached current_qps_metrics.png to show the 24-hr pattern.

We can do Tue 2/16 10:00am PT for the technical kickoff — that works for our infra lead.

Also: can Redwood handle a small routing rule where model variants with quantization are used only for background jobs (non-streaming)? We want to preserve quality on streaming paths.

Ethan
Ethan Cole
Head of Platform Engineering, DataWorks
ethan.cole@dataworks.io
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Discovery follow-up: streaming bottlenecks and p95/concurrency goals (DataWorks)

Forwarding DataWorks recap + metrics (see attachment they sent).

Primary ask: we need a compact trial proposal that addresses: dedicated capacity sizing for the trial, streaming-config recommendations (max batch window, partial-token flush policy), and a test harness timeline.

Key constraints from Ethan:
- p95 target <= 300ms for 512-token streaming (US).
- Streaming cadence target ~50–100ms per incremental chunk.
- Sustained concurrency 300, burst to 500 for 30–45s.
- Quantized model variants must not be used for streaming outputs (routing rule).

Other notes: procurement will likely request SOC2 evidence and a short DPA. Please include a short procurement roadmap (what we can provide without legal) and an initial sticker price for the 2-week tech trial.

Can you draft the trial doc by EOD and I’ll send it to Ethan tomorrow morning?

Thanks — Aisha

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery follow-up: streaming bottlenecks and p95/concurrency goals (DataWorks)

Thanks Aisha — I’ll take point on the trial proposal. High-level suggested plan below; I attached trial_proposal.pdf and bench_config.yaml for details.

1) Trial scope (2 weeks)
- Dedicated: 2x A100-equivalent hosts per shard (start with 2 shards), pinned to US-WEST region.
- Runtime config: continuous small-window batching (max batch wait 8ms, max batch size tuned by QPS), and explicit partial-token flush policy at 50–80ms cadence when tokens are generated.
- KV prefix caching: seed with hot prefixes from their sample_payloads; measure cold-miss cost.

2) Acceptance criteria (end of trial)
- p95 <= 300ms for 512-token streaming baseline on traceable test runs.
- Streaming partial-chunk cadence <= 100ms on 95% of tokens.
- Sustained 300 concurrency with <10% degradation vs baseline throughput; burst to 500 for 45s with graceful degradation (rate-limit + fallback to non-quantized model).

3) Test harness & timeline
- Day 0: ingest their sample payloads + run 3 baseline sweeps (<500 requests each).
- Day 2–4: iterate batching/flush policy and KV cache sizing; run targeted p95 stress tests.
- Day 5–10: run sustained-concurrency tests and run a simulated marketing-burst test.
- Day 11–14: regression & handoff; deliver results + ops runbook.

Procurement & security
- We can provide SOC2 Type II summary + DPA template; full reports provided under NDA.
- For KMS: support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via standard integrations; note: for private deployments we'll need explicit provisioning lead time.

Pricing ballpark: two-week dedicated PoC (capacity + SRE support + consult) — ballpark $45k–65k depending on shard count. Pricing will be refined after we validate QPS and resource utilization.

Next action: Aisha to send to Ethan tomorrow AM with proposed kickoff Wed/Tue slot (we had Tue 2/16 10:00am PT from Ethan). I’ll prepare a 30-min tech kickoff invite and include bench_config.yaml.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
